parts.text:
Analyze the attached multi-view images of a mechanical/CAD part, plus the
STEP B-rep analysis report that follows the images. Orthographic views are
labelled +X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, -Z (CAD look directions). Isometric views iso1
and iso2 are included when available.

Produce a single JSON object (model.json). Follow these steps in order.

1. SEMANTIC ORIENTATION
   The provided orthographic images are labelled according to the CAD
   coordinate system using +X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, and -Z. These labels describe
   geometric viewing directions only and must NOT initially be interpreted as
   semantic directions such as front, back, left, right, top, or bottom.

   Analyse the complete model across all provided views and determine whether
   the object has a distinguishable semantic orientation based on its
   geometry, structure, functional features, symmetry, and likely mechanical
   use.

   For each semantic direction — front, back, left, right, top, and bottom:
   - Determine whether that direction can be meaningfully identified for this
     object.
   - If identifiable, map it to one of the CAD axes: +X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, or -Z.
   - Provide a confidence score between 0 and 1.
   - Opposing semantic directions must map to opposing CAD directions. For
     example, if top = +Z, then bottom = -Z.
   - Do NOT force a semantic direction when there is insufficient evidence.
   - If a semantic direction cannot be reliably determined, assign it null.
     Do not automatically equate an unresolved semantic direction with a CAD
     axis.

   After this step, you may use the mapped semantic names (when not null)
   when describing location. Always keep the CAD axis labels available as
   the geometric ground truth.

2. FEATURE IDENTIFICATION
   List distinct functional features (mounting points, joints, interfaces)
   and structural features (ribs, shells, spines, cavities) visible across
   the views.

3. SECTIONING
   Divide the part into logical sections. For each section, capture: a short
   name, its relative location on the part, and a plain-language description
   of its geometry. Assign a unique RGB colour for each section (0–255 per
   channel). Colours must be visually distinct from one another.

4. FUNCTIONAL INTENT AND PHYSICAL BEHAVIOR
   For each section, reason about the FUNCTIONAL INTENT and the PHYSICAL
   BEHAVIOR of the section that performs that function.

5. RELATIONSHIPS
   Analyse the relationships between sections. Two types of relationships
   should be considered.
   First, functional relationships. Examples:
   transmits_load, locates_mating_part, seals_against, guides_motion,
   provides_clearance, constrains_dof, mounts_to, distributes_stress.
   Second, structural relationships. Examples:
   shares_face, adjacent_to, coaxial_with, attached_to, contained_in,
   supports, blends_into, offset_from.

6. MAJOR SURFACE INVENTORY
   Within each section, identify the MAJOR surfaces that are visually
   distinguishable across the views (distinct flat facets, distinct
   curved/cylindrical patches, especially fillet bands and chamfers) — not a
   full CAD B-rep face count. Assign each face a unique 4-digit code (0000,
   0001, ...) sequential across the whole part. Give each face a short name
   and one-line description. Note this is not an exact topological face count
   (which would typically be much higher due to small fillet/blend faces
   invisible in shaded renders), but include as many faces as you can.

7. ADJACENCY ORDERING
   Within each section's surface list, order the surfaces so each is
   physically adjacent to its neighbors in the list (a walk across the
   section, not an arbitrary order). If a section contains disconnected
   sub-groups (e.g. two separate tabs that don't touch), order each
   sub-group internally.

8. MATCH MAJOR FACES TO THE STEP REPORT
   A STEP file analysis report is also provided as a .txt file. It lists
   FACE records (and EDGE records) of this B-rep model. Match each major
   face you identified to the corresponding STEP face and record its unique
   id as Brep_id in the form "FACE N" (e.g. "FACE 0"). Use geometry type,
   area, normals, centers, and adjacent edges when they help disambiguate.

9. MINOR FACES
   For STEP faces that were not matched to a major face, categorise them
   into the section where they most likely belong. List their B-rep ids
   from the STEP analysis report as minor_faces_Brep_id for each section.
   Every FACE id from the STEP report should appear exactly once, either as
   a major_faces[].Brep_id or in some section's minor_faces_Brep_id.

OUTPUT FORMAT (JSON, model.json, no markdown fences, use this schema):
{
  "part": {
    "name": "",
    "description": "",
    "source_views": ["+Z", "-Z", "-X", "+X", "+Y", "-Y", "iso1", "iso2"],
    "semantic_orientation": {
      "front": {"cad_axis": "+Z", "confidence": 0.0},
      "back": {"cad_axis": "-Z", "confidence": 0.0},
      "left": {"cad_axis": "-X", "confidence": 0.0},
      "right": {"cad_axis": "+X", "confidence": 0.0},
      "top": {"cad_axis": "+Y", "confidence": 0.0},
      "bottom": {"cad_axis": "-Y", "confidence": 0.0}
    },
    "symmetry_note": ""
  },
  "Section": [
    {
      "id": "",
      "name": "",
      "features included": [],
      "function intent": "",
      "physical behavior": "",
      "geometry": "",
      "location": "",
      "colour": {"R": 0, "G": 0, "B": 0},
      "major_faces": [
        {"face_code": "0000", "name": "", "Brep_id": "FACE 0", "description": ""}
      ],
      "minor_faces_Brep_id": ["FACE 1", "FACE 2"],
      "relationships": [
        {
          "source id": "",
          "target id": "",
          "function relationship": "",
          "structural relationship": ""
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

For semantic_orientation, set cad_axis to null (and confidence to 0) when
that semantic direction cannot be identified. Do not invent an axis.

Labeled multi-view images of the original part follow. The STEP B-rep analysis report follows after the images.
